intro: The Onin War, sparked by a feud over the Ashikaga shogun's heir, swept the land in a storm of war. Sons slew fathers and vassals their lords: the age of gekokujo had come. In May 1534 Oda Nobuhide, lord of Furuwatari Castle in Owari, had a son, Kipposhi. As Oda Nobunaga, he would rise to the brink of ruling the realm...

Head of the Oda after his father's death, Nobunaga slew Deputy Constable Oda Nobutomo, moved to Kiyosu and set out to unite Owari. But in April 1556 his father-in-law Dosan fell to his son Yoshitatsu's revolt, and in August his own brother Nobuyuki rose against him. To unite Owari, Nobuyuki must die...

Nobunaga marched on Kyoto with Ashikaga Yoshiaki and made him shogun. But Yoshiaki, knowing himself a puppet, urged the daimyo to bring Nobunaga down. In April 1570, as Nobunaga marched on Asakura Yoshikage in Echizen, word came that his sister's husband Azai Nagamasa had turned on him. His greatest peril was at hand...

Nobunaga drove Yoshiaki from Kyoto and crushed the Asakura, the Azai and the Honganji one by one. In February 1582 Kiso Yoshimasa, Takeda Shingen's son-in-law, offered to submit. Seeing the Takeda in decline, Nobunaga accepted and ordered his heir Nobutada to attack them. No foe seemed left to stand before him...

Betrayed by his vassal Akechi Mitsuhide, Nobunaga died in the flames of the Honnoji. Mitsuhide fell to Hashiba Hideyoshi and was killed in flight. Half a month later a council met at Kiyosu to choose an heir and divide his lands. There Shibata Katsuie and Hideyoshi clashed over the heir. War between them was certain...

The strife born of the Onin War spread ever wider. In Kai, Takeda Harunobu (Shingen) exiled his father Nobutora and took the house. In Oshu the feud of Date Tanemune and his son Harumune drew the lords around them into war. Meanwhile Saito Dosan, vassal of Mino Constable Toki Yoriaki, began to pursue his ambition...

As his armies swept toward uniting the realm, Oda Nobunaga was betrayed by Akechi Mitsuhide at the Honnoji and died. Mitsuhide's hold was far from firm, and the home provinces were in chaos. In Harima, Hashiba Hideyoshi heard of Nobunaga's death and vowed to avenge his lord. The battle for the realm was about to begin...

Imagawa Yoshimoto of Suruga and Totomi made the Matsudaira of Mikawa his vassals and pressed into Owari. Saito Dosan of Mino eyed Owari too, and within it Deputy Constable Oda Nobutomo backed Constable Shiba Yoshimune against Oda Nobuhide. In 1546, at Nagoya Castle, his heir Kipposhi came of age as Saburo Nobunaga...

Years after taking the head of the Oda, Nobunaga had slain his brother Nobuyuki and Oda Nobukata of Iwakura and united Owari. But in 1560 Imagawa Yoshimoto, lord of Suruga, Totomi and Mikawa, set out for Kyoto to aid the shogun. Against his 40,000 men Nobunaga had only 4,000. All thought the Oda were doomed...

Nobunaga raced east and west to break the encirclement woven by Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki. But his ally Tokugawa Ieyasu was crushed by Takeda Shingen at Mikatagahara, and Yoshiaki rose openly against him. At his darkest hour, news came that changed everything: Takeda Shingen had died of illness at Komaba in Shinano...

Spared an invasion by the Honnoji Incident, Chosokabe Motochika took Awa and Sanuki, beat the Kono of Iyo in spring 1585 and united Shikoku. Hashiba Hideyoshi, bent on uniting the realm, ordered him to return Sanuki and Iyo. Motochika refused. In June 1585 Hideyoshi resolved to invade and called his lords to war...

On Toyotomi Hideyoshi's death his heir Hideyori, aged six, took his place. But the two who should guard him, Tokugawa Ieyasu of the warrior faction and Ishida Mitsunari of the civil faction, grew ever more bitter. In March 1599 Maeda Toshiie, the elder who had kept both sides in check, followed Hideyoshi to the grave...

Victorious at Sekigahara, Tokugawa Ieyasu became shogun and ruled from Edo. The Toyotomi protested but did nothing, letting the years slip by. Then in July 1614 word reached them that Ieyasu was in a rage: the bell of the Hokoji in Kyoto bore an inscription said to curse him...

In the late 16th century, with Japan torn by war, heroes of ages past have returned. Generals of the Three Kingdoms, warriors of the Mongol Empire: legends who shine like stars now seek fame once more and claim the realm. Daimyo against heroes of old - who will rule the realm? Never has Japan been so tense...
